abstract: The expected expansion of IoT networks and their virtualisation require improved quality of service. This paper introduces enhancements to the simulation product for 6LoWPAN networks proposed by authors, which enables service quality research. The influence of different algorithms for prioritising traffic on throughput, delay, packet delivery ratio and packet loss ratio considered.

articleTitle: Influence of Power Line Parameters on the Configuration of the Magnetic Field Distribution in its Vicinity
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The paper presents some results, obtained in the parameterized numerical modeling of magnetic field distribution created in the vicinity of high voltage power line. The accent in the study is analysis of the influence of some design and regime parameters of the transmission line on the configuration of the magnetic field distribution. The investigations are based on FEM modeling of quasi-stationary magnetic field for different values of parameters defining geometric design and currents of the three-phase power line. The field distribution has been analyzed and dependencies have been obtained between the maximum of the field values, their location relative to the axis of the three-wire line and the values of the examined line parameters.

articleTitle: A Study of the Short-Circuit Thermal Effect on Aluminum and Cooper Bus-Bars Using a Laboratory Test System
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: This paper presents a study of the short-circuit induced thermal action in bus-bars with a rectangular cross-section. The laboratory test system used in the study is designed for both analytical and experimental studies. When a current flows through the bus-bars, power and energy losses occur in the conductors. These energy losses cause heating of conductors and different parts in electrical machines and apparatus. Such problem requires a distinctive calculation of these power losses and the heating transfer regimes. The temperature measurement is performed with an embedded sensor in the lab model and also with an external thermal imaging camera.

articleTitle: Coordination of the Thermal Insulation in an Electric Resistance Furnace for Art Glass Melting
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: Various thermal insulation materials are used for the thermal insulation of electric glass melting furnaces. Their diversity makes it difficult to determine the optimum variant of multilayer insulation in order to achieve maximum energy efficiency and operational reliability of the device. The purpose of the paper is to offer, through theoretical analysis of the temperature field and losses in different types of insulating materials, optimal variant for the selection of materials and geometric dimensions of thermal insulation of art glass melting resistance furnace.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability Analysis of Kosovo Power System Local Area
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: This paper presents voltage stability analysis of Kosovo power system local area including the 35kV overhead power line from Substation(SS) Prizreni 110/35/10kV to SS Dragashi 35/10kV. In this work, the maximum load capability limit is determined using several static analysis methods. Initially, the maximum limit is calculated using the P-V and Q-V curve methods. Then in order to find out the causes of voltage instability a modal analysis is performed to identify the critical buses and branches using their nodal and branch participation factors.

articleTitle: Application of Laser Build-Up Welding for Repair of Die Casting Molds
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: This paper deals with investigation of the possibility for application of laser build-up welding for repairing of die casting molds. The surfaces of the molds, made of 1.2365 (32 CrMoV12-28) and 1.2453 (X130W5) steels, (DIN) are buildup welded by additional material of maraging alloy with a chemical composition 0.02C-19.3Ni-0.4V-2Cr-14.5CO-4.7Mo0.25Al-0.2Mn-0.2Si (wt%) and respectively nickel based alloy 73.8Ni-19.5Cr-2.8Mn-1.9Fe-2.5Nb. Some aspects of applying the build-up welding in practice are discussed. As a result of the present investigation, conclusions are made about the application of a specific additional material in the process of build-up welding depending on the alloy melting temperature.

articleTitle: Study of a Coupled Piezo-Electromagnetic Harvester
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The paper presents a study of a coupled piezoelectromagnetic harvester, consisting of a piezo-harvester and an attached to it electromagnetic harvester. Modeling in ANSYS has been performed, by means of which the horizontal deviation of the mechanical system has been obtained and the accumulated charge on the electrodes of the piezo-harvester has been calculated. The magnetic field of the electromagnetic harvester has been modeled with the help of FEMM and its electromotive force (e.m.f.) has been defined. Equivalent circuits have been drawn and experiments for validation of the developed models have been conducted.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis and Design of Lighting Equipment
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The thermal regime of the assembly determines the reliability and the efficiency of LED equipment. The ability to calculate precisely the temperature distribution of the luminaire at different stages of its design is extremely precious for the designer team. The available engineering approaches for the analysis of the thermal regime of LED luminaires at design time are discussed in the paper. The special attention is paid to their precision and the parameters that influence it. Some considerations about the tuning of the numerical thermal models, based on the author's experience are presented and supported with experimental results.

articleTitle: Dynamic modeling of "KOSOVO A" power station synchronous generator
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: This paper presents dynamic three-phase d-q axis modeling and simulation of "KOSOVO A" power station synchronous generator intended for transient analysis and relay protections parameters determination, taking into account the static and dynamic interactions between stator and rotor. A simplified and computationally efficient five order mathematical model is developed under the assumption that the Kirchhoff laws and the network equations are written as for stationary state. The generator is analyzed in "abc" coordinates to describe the physical inherent of three-phase short circuit. A system of differential equations representing the dynamic behavior of the machine is developed and implemented in Matlab/Simulink. The proposed model and case study provide important and valuable results for the generator relay protection settings, allowing an easy setup of the relay protections parameters by referring the results obtained in this work.

articleTitle: Variational Approach with Transferring Coefficients for Magnetic Circuit Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: This paper introduces the possibility for application of the variational approach with transferring coefficients for analysis of linear and non-linear magnetic circuits operating at constant regimes. The method is based on a specific theorem for variational analysis of electric circuits. The theorem is reformed analogically for magnetic circuits, which helps the application of the variational approach with transferring coefficients for analysis of magnetic circuits. Limited practical examples for variational analysis of linear and non-linear magnetic circuits, operating at constant regimes are presented to illustrate the proposed method.

Author Keywords: analysis of linear and non-linear magnetic circuits
methodology for variational analysis of magnetic circuits

articleTitle: Analysis of the Performance of AQ500 SODARs in Low Temperature Conditions
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: This paper discusses the specifics of the operation of the AQ500 SODAR system in low temperature conditions. Special attention is paid to the power supply of the system during the winter period and its influence on quality of the signal. The impact of the battery charging cycles on the quality of the signal is investigated in real operating conditions of the system.

articleTitle: Attempt to a Video-Transmission Capability in MV Mine Cable Network Using BPL-PLC Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: This article presents and discusses the attempt to transmit video content using the BPL-PLC (Broadband over Power Line - Power Line Communication) technology. It includes simulation results of a specially developed digital transmitter and receiver, dedicated to a given predefined 6 kV mining power cable. The effect of two different transmission modes (2-7 MHz and 3-7.5 MHz) and two types of coupling (capacitive-inductive and induction-inductive), on the quality of bi-directional transmission, was also examined. The quality assessment of transmitted content, including both QoS (Quality of Service) and QoE (Quality of Experience) approaches, was evaluated on a set of samples processed in different resolution, namely: 480x270, 768x432, and 1280x720. Based on this, conclusions have been formulated, regarding the expected efficiency, as well as guidelines for further video transmission tests, including real-time mining conditions.

articleTitle: Impact of the Treatment Media Conductivity on the Thermal Effects in Plant Cellular Materials During PEF Processing
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The object of investigation in the present work are the thermal effects that occur in plant materials during the pulsed electric field treatment for assisting the process of extraction of specific oils. The aim of the study is to analyze the influence that the properties of the solution in which the material is being processed have on the thermal field configuration in the studied cell tissue. The distribution of the electric field, the currents and corresponding Joule losses, the temperatures and the temperature gradients are determined and compared for several solvents with different conductivity. The analysis of the coupled electric and thermal processes is carried out on the basis of fields modeling using the finite element method. Regions of special attention are the areas of neighborhood between two cells where the processes are modeled in two steps: before and after electroporation on the basis of corresponding changes in the size and conducting properties of the contact zone.

articleTitle: Identification of a DC Motor with Independent Excitation
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: New approach based on wavelet functions is applied for identification of the parameters of a DC motor with independent excitation in the paper. Coiflet wavelets are used for this purpose. The parameters estimated by the identification are compared with the analytically determined values. The relative parameter errors and relative output errors are calculated, and the adequateness of the obtained mathematical model is evaluated. The results are analyzed, and corresponding conclusions are made.

articleTitle: Determination of the Leakege Parameters of Synchronous Hydrogenerators
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: An application of FEM for studying the leakage of stator slots of synchronous hydrogenerators is presented. The approach presented takes into account the saturation of the stator teeth and the mutual influence of the current in adjacent stator slots. Results for leakage inductance and emf due to the slot leakage are obtained for 2 MW and 4 MW synchronous hydro generators.

articleTitle: Integrated Systems for the Continuous Monitoring of the Technical Condition of Transformer Units
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The monitoring of the condition and the diagnostic of transformer units is a constant endeavor, continuously adapted to meet the demands of transport operators. The requirements for the achievement of integrated systems for the monitoring and diagnostic of transformer units are delivered through specifications and norms establishing a set of parameters and the conditions necessary for the monitoring and diagnostic, as well as the characteristics of the monitoring and diagnostic software. The aging of the oil-impregnated cellulose insulation and the loss of tensile strength are important factors limiting the lifespan of transformers. The system architecture is open, allowing specific configurations to be developed for each monitored transformer unit. The paper also shows the importance of improving the accuracy for identifying as early as possible the degradation of the cellulose insulation related to the transformer units, by integrating two chemical markers - methanol (MeOH) and 2 furaldehyde (2-FAL) into the structure of the monitoring systems, which can provide correlated information about the aging condition of the solid insulation in oil transformers.

articleTitle: Adaptive Boundary Control Technique of Distributed Parameter Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: This paper presents adaptive boundary optimal temperature control of a reinforced concrete plate. The plate is modeled by a parabolic partial differential equation. Different algorithms have been studied for online parameter identification for optimal adaptive control of heat transfer systems. Control problems for distributed parameter systems, described by parabolic PDEs have been investigated.

articleTitle: Research into the Possibilities for Diagnosis of Asynchronous Electric Drives Powered by a Frequency Inverter in the Presence of Unbalance
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The paper explores the possibilities for unbalance identification in a three-phase squirrel-cage asynchronous motor using a stator current spectrum analysis (MSCA) and a standardised method for diagnosis of dynamic eccentricity determined by frequency control and different modes of operation. Several experimental tests were performed on a real physical model of electric drive, creating, thereby, the necessary means for applying MSCA and carrying out a comparative analysis based on conventional schematic diagram and frequency regulation. The results obtained reveal some practical methods of MSCA implementation upon frequency response adjustment measurements and significant non-sinusoidality of the supply voltage.

articleTitle: Modeling of Thermal Transient Processes in Frequency-controlled Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The paper presents a model of thermal transients in induction motor controlled via a variable frequency drive, which takes into account the operation of the motor at speeds different than the rated one. Experimental recording of motor heating curves at different angular speeds has been done, to verify the model.

articleTitle: A Multisensor Environmental Monitoring Device
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: We present an air monitoring device capable of measuring several outdoor parameters such as ambient temperature, atmospheric pressure, relative humidity, particulate matter 2.5 and 10 micrometers and beta/gamma radiation. The device is designed, developed, manufactured, and optimized in-house. It is a building block in an environmental monitoring network of evenly distributed stations on a national level, performing monitoring on a long time scale and with high time resolution.

articleTitle: Magnetic Materials for Coaxial Magnetic Gear Torque Density Enchainment
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: In this paper are analyzed different soft and hard magnetic materials for coaxial magnetic gears torque enhancement. Estimation of material properties impact over the magnetic gear input and output torques is implemented by finite element method model. The modelling is carried out by Ansys-Maxwell software. Presented results comparison is very useful for design optimization of coaxial magnetic gears and torque and power densities enhancement.

articleTitle: Implementation of the Phase Compensation Approach for Tuning Power System Stabilizers with Simulink
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the capabilities of the Simulink simulation environment for tuning the parameters of Power system stabilizers (PSS), which play a key role in damping the low-frequency oscillations in the electric power systems. First, the theory and algorithms for optimization of the parameters are examined, focusing on the phase compensation (P-Vr) method, which was selected and implemented in Simulink. The different steps of the tuning algorithm are explained, as well as the formulation of the objective function. The theoretically described steps were practically applied to a single-machine system, as well as to the well-known four-machine system of Kundur. The available solvers were also tested and compared in terms of speed and efficiency.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of Variable Speed Induction Motor Drive with Fault Tree Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: A model for assessment of the reliability, of a variable speed drive with an induction motor, is presented in the paper. The relationship between the causes of failures and their effects on the drive system has been analyzed using failure modes and effects analysis (FMEA) and fault tree analysis (FTA).

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effect of Soil Thermal Resistivity on High-Voltage Cables Sizing
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The determination of the ampacity of high voltage cables is most often done by standard, rather than measured values of soil thermal resistivity, as shown by a study published in a CIGRE technical brochure [1]. Since the sizing approach is generally conservative, cables tend to operate far below their transmission capacity [2]. The progressive increase of load, as well as the employment of cables in bulk power transmission requires a good knowledge of their thermal behavior as early as at the design stage, and the large capital investments require their optimum operation and the use of their full transmission capacity without risk of thermal failure. This paper presents case studies on the sensitivity of cable ampacity to soil thermal resistivity and analyzes the need for experimental verification to more accurately identify the initial computational conditions [3].

articleTitle: Studying the Operating Modes of a Current Source DC/DC Converter with Voltage Clamping Across Resonant Capacitor and Different Designs of the High Frequency Transformer
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: This paper examines the operation of a current source inverter used as a DC-DC converter with voltage clamping across resonant capacitor (CSVCRC). The converter is intended for charging energy storage elements, such as supercapacitors. The examination of the converter is performed with respect to different constructions of the high frequency transformer. Two arrangements of the transformer windings are presented - transformer with sectioned windings and interleaved windings. The results show that an asymmetry into the primary windings influence the operating mode of the converter.

articleTitle: Study of Two- and Four- Spring Electromagnetic Harvesters
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The paper presents a study of two- and four- spring electromagnetic harvesters, consisting of Π-shaped plates with 4 magnets mounted on two or four springs, rigidly fixed at their low ends. A coil is placed between the magnets. Modeling by means of ANSYS has been performed and the horizontal deviation of the mechanical system has been obtained. The magnetic fields of the electromagnetic harvesters have been modeled by means of FEMM. Their electromotive forces (e.m.f.) and power have been defined. Experiments for validating the models have been conducted.

articleTitle: Study of Operational Parameters of a Capacitor Bank with Detuned Reactor for Power Factor Correction in a Low Voltage Network
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The paper presents the results from a study of a capacitor bank with detuned reactor for power factor correction in a three-phase low voltage network. The effect of the high harmonics in the network, as well as the influence of the inductance of the detuned reactor on the operational parameters of the three-phase capacitor bank have been studied by means of a computer model, synthesized in Matlab/Simulink. The parameters of the network have been taken into account. The studies have been performed at the following values of capacitive power of the capacitor bank: 10kVAr, 30kVAr, 50kVAr and 60kVAr. Conclusions have been made and recommendations given concerning the choice of a detuned reactor for power factor correction devices.

articleTitle: Development of a Cost-effective High Accuracy Multi-channel RTD Signal Conditioner
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The paper discusses the development and testing of a multi-channel RTD signal conditioner designed to study hybrid heating and cooling systems, which include two or more energy sources: solid fuel boiler; heat pump system and/or solar collectors. An "Expansion card" has been developed to increase the number of the analogue RTD channels provided by DAQ-board LabJack UE9 and to ensure high accuracy of temperature measurements at the price about 0.5 Euro per channel.

articleTitle: Starting Regime of an Electronic Startup Regulating Apparatus for Fluorescent Lamps
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: It has been studied the starting regime of an electronic startup regulating apparatus (ESRA) with specialized integrated circuit which provides regulation of the starting process. The study is carried out at different regimes of two fluorescent lamps. It has been studied also a mode of an unidirectional conductivity of the FL. The parameters of the ESRA were determined using the software product "Ballast Designer" of International Rectifier Company. There were performed simulation studies within the PSpice programme environment for specific intervals of the FL's starting mode. The current and voltage of the FL were determined during the different stages of electrodes' heating.

articleTitle: Simulating and Estimating the Nonsinusoidality of Current and Voltage during the Operation of an Adjustable-Frequency Electric Drive and Capacitor Banks
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The article addresses matters concerned with application of computer simulation for rationally selecting the parameters and installation places of controlled capacitor banks in a network containing an adjustable-frequency electric drive. The adopted solutions are based on estimating the total harmonic distortion of voltage. In the case considered, the frequency-adjustable drive operates in a repeated short-term mode. A conclusion about the effectiveness of using the computer simulation methods for such case is drawn.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Starting Mode of a Three-phase Induction Machine with Single-phase Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The starting mode of a three-phase induction machine with single-phase power supply has been investigated. Expressions have been obtained to determine the stator current phasor for all slip values. Several results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: FOP - FSM Measurement – Relative Position of the Test Conductors
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: Experimental evaluation of the measurement results based on FSM (Frequency Shift Method) concept in the non-conventional FOP (Fall-of-Potential) measuring scheme, for different angles between the test conductors, is presented in this paper. As it is well known, the optimal angle between the test conductors is θ = 90°. However, in practice, most often because of the physical obstacles in the surround substation, this condition cannot be provided. We have experimentally determined that the angle between the test conductors must be less than 60° relative to the optimal angle θ. In that case the corresponding measurement error is less than 3%.

articleTitle: Application of Current Transformers in Power Electronics Converters with Voltage Feedback
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: The article presents a solution through a current transformer (or a transformer that operates in current mode), which provides galvanic separation of the signal between the control unit and the power unit, in power electronic converters. The design of this specific current transformer is introduced. The magnetic core of the current transformer is chosen to be toroidal. The design recommendations for selecting the appropriate magnetic core material are discussed. The soft magnetic materials as nanocrystalline materials and amorphous alloys with flat hysteresis loops meet the design requirements. The errors of the current transformer are estimated. Some other specific applications of current transformers are also presented.

articleTitle: Power System Stabilizers for Inverter Dominated Future Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 21st International Symposium on Electrical Apparatus & Technologies (SIELA)
abstract: This paper proposes implementation of power system stabilizer (PSS) function in inverters for stabilizing low frequency power oscillations in future inverter dominated power systems (PS). It considers several concepts and solutions for PSS taking into account the expected characteristics of the future power systems with high share of renewable energy sources. Implementation of inverters with PSS function is proposed for stabilizing low frequency power oscillations. Several classical PSS types are studied to outline the essence of the process and to examine the potential for their implementation in inverters. For design and conditioning purposes, small signal stability analysis model is first used. Nonlinear simulation using Matlab/Simulink is applied on a single machine infinite bus system (SMIB) to show the performance of different PSS types in enhancement of power system dynamics. A ΔP PSS Simulink model is constructed. A comparison between ΔP, Δω and multiband PSS under various disturbance conditions is performed to evaluate the effectiveness of the examined model and to validate the applicability of the approach. The functional requirements and characteristics of the inverter based PSS are evaluated and tested using literature analysis and laboratory experiments performed at the Power System Stability Laboratory of TU-Sofia.
